title: Injective normalization systems and faithful flatness over finite algebraic stages
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], and let $P/K$ be algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-element]. Let $I$ be the set of intermediate fields $K\subseteq F\subseteq P$ finite-dimensional over $K$, ordered by inclusion. For $Q=F\in I$ or $Q=P$, put $E_Q=(L\otimes_KQ)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $R_Q=\overline A^{\,Q}$, $C_Q=\overline B^{\,E_Q}$ and $T_Q=B\otimes_AR_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the bar denotes integral closure, and reduction is quotient by all nilpotents. All transition maps are induced by field inclusions and multiplication. Then $I$ is nonempty and directed, the transition maps on $E_Q,R_Q,C_Q$ are injective, and the canonical maps
$$\varinjlim_{F\in I}R_F\longrightarrow R_P,\qquad \varinjlim_{F\in I}C_F\longrightarrow C_P,\qquad \varinjlim_{F\in I}T_F\longrightarrow T_P$$
are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every $F\in I$, $R_F\to R_P$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. If $a$ and $b$ are uniformizers of $A$ and $B$, respectively, then $R_F[1/a]=F$ canonically, and the multiplication map $T_F[1/b]\to E_F$ is surjective [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. A uniformizer means a generator of the maximal ideal. The map $T_Q\to C_Q$ makes $C_Q$ integral over $T_Q$. No Noetherianity of $R_P$, finiteness of $C_P/T_P$, essential finite type of $B/A$, or separability is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, paragraph beginning By construction, the field ... is a filtered colimit; transition-system refinement written by the agent. Faithful flatness uses Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1), together with Krull-Akizuki and integral lying-over in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Finite supports of fields. The field $K$ belongs to $I$. Given $F,G\in I$, choose finite $K$-bases of both. Their union consists of finitely many elements of the algebraic extension $P/K$, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] makes the field they generate finite over $K$. It contains $F$ and $G$, proving directedness. The same lemma applied to one element shows that every $x\in P$ belongs to some $F\in I$. Thus $P=\bigcup_F F$. All intermediate fields are subsets of the fixed set $P$, so this is a small directed index set in a universe containing $P$.

source.place: Tag 09GH, lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated; application to the filtered finite subfields in Tag 09II

proof.text:
Injectivity of the reduced tensor diagram. For intermediate fields $F\subseteq G\subseteq P$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives inverse maps
$$(L\otimes_K F)\otimes_F G\longrightarrow L\otimes_K G,\quad (l\otimes f)\otimes g\longmapsto l\otimes fg,$$
and $l\otimes g\mapsto(l\otimes1)\otimes g$; the balancing relations and pure tensors verify both compositions. Under this identification the raw transition is scalar extension along $F\subseteq G$, hence injective by [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective]. If a raw tensor $z$ becomes nilpotent after this injection, some $z^n$ maps to zero, so $z^n=0$. Consequently the induced transition $E_F\to E_G$ is injective, also for $G=P$. Field inclusions give injective maps $R_F\to R_G$; the injections $E_F\to E_G$ restrict to injective maps $C_F\to C_G$, because the same monic polynomial over $B$ still vanishes [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. These maps preserve identities and compositions since their formulas do.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, filtered-normalization paragraph; explicit injectivity refinement

proof.text: The first normalization colimit. If $x\in R_P$, Step 1 places $x$ in some finite field $F\subseteq P$. A monic equation for $x$ over $A$ is an equality already in $F$, since $F\to P$ is injective. Thus $x\in R_F$, proving $R_P=\bigcup_F R_F$. Conversely every $R_F$ maps into $R_P$ by the same monic equation [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. This union is a ring colimit: a compatible family of ring maps $h_F:R_F\to U$ defines $h(x)=h_F(x)$ for a stage containing $x$; directedness makes this independent of the choice, and computing sums and products at a common stage proves that $h$ is the unique ring map extending the family. This verifies the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and hence the first claimed canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09II, displayed colimit A prime 1 = colim A_i; expanded directed-union verification

proof.text: The second normalization colimit. Every element of $L\otimes_K P$ is a finite sum $\sum_j l_j\otimes p_j$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Step 1 puts the finitely many $p_j$ into one finite field $F$, so every element of the quotient $E_P$ comes from $E_F$. Together with Step 2 this identifies $E_P$ with the union of the injective system $E_F$. If $c\in C_P$, choose a representative $e\in E_F$ of $c$. A monic equation over $B$ annihilating $c$ also annihilates $e$: its value in $E_F$ maps to zero in $E_P$, and that map is injective. Thus $e\in C_F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Conversely an element integral over $B$ at a stage remains so in $E_P$. Therefore $C_P=\bigcup_F C_F$. The common-stage formula $h(c)=h_F(c)$ from Step 3 gives the universal ring cocone and the second canonical isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This argument does not assume that the raw tensors are reduced.

source.place: Tag 09II, displayed colimit B prime 1 = colim B_i; expanded finite-support and monic-equation descent

proof.text: The tensor colimit as rings. Let $h_F:T_F\to U$ be any compatible family of ring maps. Their restrictions along $B\to T_F$ coincide, since any two stages have a common successor; write the common map as $u:B\to U$. Their restrictions along $R_F\to T_F$ glue by Step 3 to a ring map $v:R_P\to U$. The maps $u,v$ agree on $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] there is a unique ring map $h:T_P\to U$ with $h(b\otimes r)=u(b)v(r)$. It restricts to $h_F$, since both maps agree on the two tensor factors. Conversely any extension of all $h_F$ must have these restrictions on $B$ and $R_P$, so the same tensor universal property makes it equal to $h$. This proves that the specified cocone $(T_P,(T_F\to T_P))$ is colimiting, and proves the third canonical isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No injectivity of tensor transitions is needed.

source.place: Tags 00CV and 00DD, tensor universal property and tensor-colimit argument, in the algebra diagram of Tag 09II

proof.text: The finite normalizations are Dedekind. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is a nonfield local principal ideal domain. It is Noetherian since each ideal has one generator. Choose a generator $a\ne0$ of its nonzero maximal ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], every nonzero element is a unit times a power of $a$. Any nonzero prime contains a nonzero nonunit, hence contains $a$, so it is the maximal ideal. The chain $(0)\subsetneq(a)$ therefore proves that $A$ has dimension one. For each finite $F/K$, all hypotheses of [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] now hold. Its conclusion says that $R_F$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension one. In particular it is a Dedekind domain, without requiring $R_F$ to be finite over $A$.

Faithful flatness at every finite stage. The inclusion $R_F\subseteq R_P\subseteq P$ makes $R_P$ torsion-free over $R_F$: a product of two nonzero elements in the field $P$ cannot vanish. Step 6 and [lem-sfb-dedekind-torsionfree-module-flat] show that $R_F\to R_P$ is flat. Every element of $R_P$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$, hence over $R_F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; thus this inclusion is integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] it is surjective on prime spectra. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] proves faithful flatness. Neither finite generation nor Noetherianity of the target module $R_P$ enters the argument.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1), and algebra.tex Tags 00GQ and 00HQ

proof.text:
Inverting a base uniformizer. [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] implies $A[1/a]=K$: every fraction denominator in $A$ is a unit times a power of $a$. For $x\in F\subseteq P$, algebraicity [def-weil-algebraic-element] gives a monic equation $x^n+\sum_{i<n}c_i x^i=0$ over $K$ (divide a nonzero polynomial by its leading coefficient). Choose $N\geq0$ so that every $a^N c_i\in A$. Then $y=a^N x$ satisfies
$$y^n+\sum_{i<n}c_i a^{N(n-i)}y^i=0,$$
whose coefficients belong to $A$. Thus $y\in R_F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and $x=y/a^N\in R_F[1/a]$. The comparison into $F$ is injective by the fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], since $R_F\subseteq F$ and $a\ne0$. It is therefore the claimed canonical isomorphism $R_F[1/a]\cong F$.

source.place: Tag 00PD and the monic denominator-clearing calculation underlying integral localization, Tag 0307

proof.text:
The localized multiplication map. The same unit-times-power result [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] gives $B[1/b]=L$. Since $A\to B$ is local and injective, the image of $a$ is a nonzero nonunit, so it equals $ub^e$ for a unit $u\in B$ and $e\geq1$. It is consequently invertible in $T_F[1/b]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Every raw tensor is a finite sum $\sum_j l_j\otimes x_j$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $l_j=v_j/b^{m_j}$ with $v_j\in B$ and, by Step 8, $x_j=r_j/a^{n_j}$ with $r_j\in R_F$. The element
$$\sum_j (v_j\otimes r_j)b^{-m_j}a^{-n_j}\ \in T_F[1/b]$$
maps to that raw tensor and therefore to its class in $E_F$. The multiplication map exists by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and extends to the localization since $b$ is a unit in the $L$-algebra $E_F$. This proves its surjectivity, even when $L\otimes_K F$ has nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 09II normalization tensor diagram; explicit localized multiplication calculation using Tag 00PD

proof.text: The integral map $T_Q\to C_Q$. For $Q=F$ or $P$, the image of each $r\in R_Q$ in $E_Q$ satisfies the image over $B$ of its monic equation over $A$. Thus it lies in $C_Q$; the image of $B$ also lies there, and $C_Q$ is a subring by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. These compatible maps from $B$ and $R_Q$ define the multiplication map $T_Q\to C_Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For $c\in C_Q$, a monic equation over $B$ becomes a monic equation over $T_Q$ by mapping each coefficient $v\in B$ to $v\otimes1$. It still annihilates $c$. Hence every element of $C_Q$ is integral over $T_Q$. This proves integrality of the specified map, without asserting its injectivity or finiteness.
